gen-irish-grover-gf-menbere: Sturdy, soft-edged and cheerful, Irish Grover stands tall up top while Menbere stacks its lowercase like rolled cord beneath it. One is built to be noticed; the other, a sans-serif, to be read.
gen-irish-grover-gf-mitr: Mitr keeps its capitals and lowercase almost level in height. Irish Grover above it has big, tall lowercase and a gentle stroke variation, so the sans-serif body can sit back and let it lead.
gen-irish-grover-gf-momo-trust-display: Momo Trust Display spaces its letters out in a loose, drifting way, with a generous x-height that gives each line plenty of room. Irish Grover leads above with sturdy, softly shaded forms, and the sans body would carry on easily underneath.
gen-irish-grover-gf-mukta: Irish Grover makes words look big and sturdy. It is the one to announce things with its soft, organic shading, while Mukta, a plain sans with tall-bodied small letters, simply gets on with the explaining.
gen-irish-grover-gf-mukta-mahee: Chunky, friendly and a bit playful, Irish Grover has stems that outweigh its hairlines only slightly. Mukta Mahee, a plain sans with tall, sturdy lowercase, would carry a long passage along without any fuss.
gen-irish-grover-gf-mukta-vaani: Irish Grover's tall lowercase makes every word look sturdy and large, with thick and thin strokes close enough to feel related. It handles the shouting while Mukta Vaani, a sans-serif, does the quiet explaining.
gen-irish-grover-gf-narnoor: Soft, sturdy and fun, Irish Grover sets the tone with a weight difference like thread against yarn. Narnoor, a sans with short ascenders over big bowls, gives that personality a tidy, grounded partner.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-display: Tall, friendly and a little pressed-looking, Irish Grover has diagonals slightly thinner than its verticals. Noto Sans Display answers with a big, tall middle zone in every word, so the two feel like relatives of different temperaments.
gen-irish-grover-gf-play: Play reads with a faint weight difference between upstrokes and downstrokes, and little height gap between its cases. Irish Grover is the big, sturdy voice here, while the sans-serif body simply does the steady work.
gen-irish-grover-gf-port-lligat-sans: Fun, sturdy and soft around the edges, Irish Grover brings a measured weight difference like thread against yarn. And Port Lligat Sans, a plain sans with open-sided bowls and tightly packed letters, makes the strongest contrast.
